input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay on Customer for three years expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — precisely the walk-away position under this rule, and well short of the fallback (a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised). Nothing elsewhere provides an exit: Section 8.1 fixes a three-year term and Section 9 gives only cause-based termination rights, with no convenience termination or commitment reduction. It also directly conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. We proposed the preferred position (no minimum commitment; pay for Services ordered and used), which is consistent with §§ 7.1 and 12.3, and flagged the 12-month reducible commitment with true-up as a fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year take-or-pay commitment; fees payable for Services ordered/used only
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, and it contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment. We have replaced it so Fees are payable only for Services ordered and used; if a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.

ops.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: 2.1 Customer makes no minimum purchase or volume commitment. Customer is obliged to pay only for Services ordered under an Order Form and actually used, and no take-or-pay, shortfall, or similar charge applies.
